standard.title: Relative Frequencies and Compound Probability
standard.description: calculate relative frequencies from given or collected data to estimate probabilities of events involving "and", inclusive "or" and exclusive "or"
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can list all outcomes for compound events with and without replacement and assign probabilities (AC9M9P01). They have not yet used relative frequencies from data to estimate probabilities involving compound logical connectives ('and', inclusive 'or', exclusive 'or'), or used Venn diagrams and two-way tables for this purpose.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students calculate relative frequencies to estimate probabilities of compound events involving 'and', inclusive 'or' and exclusive 'or', using Venn diagrams and two-way tables.

nodes.label: Relative frequency as a probability estimate
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can calculate relative frequencies from data and explain how they estimate theoretical probability for compound events.
nodes.minimum_width: Calculate relative frequencies for two events from a given data set; explain why a larger data set gives a more reliable probability estimate.
nodes.typical_width: Calculate relative frequencies for a range of events from given or collected data; connect long-run relative frequency to theoretical probability; use relative frequencies to make probability estimates and predictions.
wider: Investigate how large population data sets (e.g. census data, health surveys) are used to estimate population-level probabilities — discuss the role of sample size in reliability
Design and test an algorithm to calculate relative frequencies from a generated data set — evaluate reliability as the data set grows
Connect relative frequency to the frequentist interpretation of probability — contrast with classical (equally likely outcomes) probability
success_criteria: Correctly calculates relative frequency as (number of times event occurred) ÷ (total number of trials)
States that larger samples give more reliable relative frequency estimates
Uses a relative frequency to make a probability estimate for a future event

nodes.label: Compound events: 'and', inclusive 'or', exclusive 'or'
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can distinguish between 'and', inclusive 'or' and exclusive 'or' events and represent them using Venn diagrams or two-way tables.
nodes.minimum_width: Define 'and' (intersection), inclusive 'or' (union including overlap) and exclusive 'or' (union excluding overlap) for two events; represent one compound event of each type on a Venn diagram.
nodes.typical_width: Use Venn diagrams and two-way tables to represent and calculate frequencies for events involving 'and', inclusive 'or' and exclusive 'or'; correctly identify which region of the Venn diagram corresponds to each compound event; use these to estimate probabilities from data.
wider: Investigate the addition rule for probability: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B) — verify using Venn diagrams and explain why the intersection must be subtracted
Connect Venn diagram regions to set notation (intersection ∩, union ∪, complement) as a foundation for formal probability
Investigate real data contexts with overlapping categories (e.g. students who play sport AND music) using two-way tables and calculate all relevant compound probabilities

response_modes.reason: Students commonly confuse inclusive and exclusive 'or' — in everyday language 'or' is often exclusive, but in probability it is usually inclusive. Working across contexts where the distinction matters — and where both interpretations are plausible — resolves this conflation.

success_criteria: Correctly distinguishes inclusive 'or' (A ∪ B) from exclusive 'or' (A or B but not both) on a Venn diagram
Correctly identifies the region for 'A and B' (intersection) on a Venn diagram
Calculates the correct frequency/probability for each compound event type from a given data set
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who conflate inclusive and exclusive "or" assign wrong probability regions on Venn diagrams, corrupting compound probability estimates in N3. The everyday/mathematical "or" distinction must be established before estimation.

nodes.label: Estimating compound event probabilities from data
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use relative frequencies from data to estimate probabilities of compound events ('and', 'or') and use these to make predictions.
nodes.minimum_width: Use relative frequencies from a given data set to estimate the probability of one compound event involving 'and' and one involving 'or'.
nodes.typical_width: Calculate relative frequencies for a range of compound events from given or collected data; use Venn diagrams or two-way tables as tools; use estimates to make predictions; compare estimates to theoretical probabilities where these can be calculated.
wider: Design, test and refine an algorithm to calculate relative frequencies for compound events from a generated data set; evaluate reliability as the number of trials increases
Investigate a real survey data set with two categorical variables and calculate all four compound probabilities (A and B, A and not B, not A and B, not A and not B) — use a two-way table
Connect relative frequency estimates to decision-making contexts — discuss when a probability estimate is reliable enough to base a decision on

response_modes.reason: Estimating compound event probabilities from data integrates relative frequency calculation, compound event identification and Venn diagram/two-way table representation. Students who can do each step separately often make errors when they must identify the correct compound event region and then calculate the relative frequency for it.

success_criteria: Correctly calculates relative frequencies for both 'and' and 'or' compound events from the same data set
Uses a Venn diagram or two-way table to organise the data before calculating
Makes a reasonable prediction based on the estimated probability and explains the reasoning
